rules.title: Statewide prohibition on local rent control (M.G.L. c. 40P)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not pass, keep or enforce rent control, so there is no state or local legal cap on rent increases in Massachusetts. A city or town that accepts Chapter 40P may adopt only a narrow, voluntary program in which the city pays owners the gap between market rent and controlled rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to every city and town in Massachusetts. The only local rent regulation allowed is the voluntary, city-compensated kind described in § 4(a) to (c).
rules.exemptions: A city or town that accepts Chapter 40P may adopt rent control only if: (a) owners may opt out after six months; (b) it does not regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condo conversion or removal of units, and it does not apply to units of owners with fewer than ten rental units or units with a fair market rent over $400; and (c) the city pays owners the difference between market and controlled rent from its general funds.
rules.conflict_note: This is a long-settled state ban on local rent control. The records show no local rent control ordinance currently in effect that conflicts with it. A 2026 ballot initiative to repeal it (Initiative Petition 25-21) was kept off the ballot by the SJC on June 23, 2026, so the ban stays in force.
rules.reason: Merged the official statute text with a secondary source describing the same Chapter 40P ban.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21: statewide cap on rent increases (blocked from the November 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: This proposal would have limited yearly rent increases to the lower of CPI or 5% and repealed G.L. c. 40P. It is not law: on June 23, 2026 the SJC ruled it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot because it includes a religious exemption.
rules.key_value: Lesser of CPI or 5% annually (proposed; not enacted)
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to most residential rental units statewide.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; new units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; and units in facilities run only for educational, religious or nonprofit purposes.
rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units
Newly built units less than 10 years old

rules.reason: Merged two secondary sources describing the same 2026 rent-cap ballot initiative that the SJC blocked. It is kept separate from enacted law because it failed.
